turns.t: Good morning, doctor. I'm Niamh, I look after Mr Hegarty. He took a tumble on Sunday, so I thought we'd best have his tablets looked at.
Good morning, both. Mr Hegarty, how are you after the fall? ~
Grand, thank you, doctor. A bit sore, but grand. ~
Did he hit his head, Niamh?
No, thank God. He went down on his side, and no, he didn't hit his head at all.
That's the main thing, on a blood thinner. Let's go through all his medicines.
There's the apixaban, 5 mg twice a day, the blood thinner. And bisoprolol, 2.5 mg once a day.
Right. And the third?
A little yellow tablet, round, small. I give it in the morning, but I can't tell you the name, it's come out of the blister packs.
I'll check our record to see what the yellow one is. Mr Hegarty, do you know what it's for?
Something for the heart, I think. Or the water. I leave it to Niamh.
Fair enough, I'll find out and ring you. Any allergies to medicines?
None, no. He has never had a problem.
Let me ask about his other conditions.
Atrial fibrillation, which is what the blood thinner's for, high blood pressure, and arthritis in the hips.
Good. Does he manage the tablets himself? ~
I give them from the pack, morning and evening. He'd forget otherwise. ~
That's the safest way. Mr Hegarty, have you been dizzy before the fall? ~
No, I just went over the rug. The rug is a menace. ~
I told him to let me take it up. ~
Take it up, Niamh. A loose rug is a very common cause. ~
I will today. ~
Because he's on a blood thinner, any fall needs care. If he hits his head, vomits, becomes drowsy or confused, he needs the emergency department straight away, even if he seems fine.
I understand. ~
And I'd like to see him again in a week, to review the tablets, once I've found out what the yellow one is.
A week. I'll book it. Should I keep him off his feet in the meantime? ~
No, gentle walking with his stick is good for him, just not alone on the stairs. ~
I'll walk him myself, then. ~
Mr Hegarty, mind that rug. ~
I will, doctor. Thank you. ~

chief_complaint.value: He took a tumble on Sunday

clinical_uncertainties.description: Carer cannot name one tablet and describes it as little, yellow and round; patient does not know what it is for.

clinical_actions.description: Safety-net: emergency department if head strike, vomiting, drowsiness or confusion after a fall on a blood thinner
